test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

He looked extremely smart and __handsomest__ in the black suit.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the phrase "**extremely smart and handsomest**," which contains an error in **degree of comparison**.
 
• The word "**handsomest**" is the superlative form of "handsome" and should only be used when comparing more than two or when preceded by "the."
 
• However, the sentence uses the **intensifier** "extremely," which is typically used with adjectives in the **positive degree**, not superlative.
 
• Therefore, the grammatically correct and meaningful form is "**extremely smart and handsome**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He looked extremely smart and **handsome** in the black suit."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Do not use **superlative adjectives** (e.g., handsomest) with intensifiers like "extremely," "very," or "so." Use the **positive degree** instead.
 
• "Extremely handsome" and "the most handsome" are both correct depending on the structure, but they cannot be combined improperly.
